metadata.title: BSG/BASL/BSIR Guidelines for the Management of Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) in Adults
metadata.organization: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG), British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL), British Society of Interventional Radiology (BSIR)

epidemiology.incidence: HCC is the sixth most common malignancy and third most common cause of cancer-related death worldwide

uk_data.incidence_rate: 6 per 100,000 in the UK, with rates increasing
uk_data.annual_cases: Approximately 6,100 new cases annually in the UK

target_population.group: All patients with cirrhosis of any aetiology who would be fit for treatment
Patients with chronic HBV infection with significant fibrosis (F3) or family history of HCC
Patients with chronic HBV infection from endemic regions

modality.notes: AFP is not recommended as a standalone surveillance tool
modality.quality: Surveillance ultrasound should achieve visualisation of at least 80% of the liver

surveillance.exclusion: Surveillance should not be offered to patients with Child-Pugh C cirrhosis unless awaiting liver transplantation

modality.name: CT/MRI
modality.criteria: Arterial phase hyperenhancement (APHE) and washout in the portal venous or delayed phase
modality.specificity: Greater than 95% for HCC in cirrhotic liver
modality.li_rads: LI-RADS classification recommended for nodules detected on surveillance

modality.name: CEUS
modality.role: Can be used for characterisation of nodules detected on surveillance ultrasound

biopsy.indication: For atypical lesions or when considering systemic therapy where diagnosis affects treatment
biopsy.note: Needle track seeding risk is approximately 2.7% (meta-analysis)

afp.note: AFP greater than 400 ng/mL is highly suggestive of HCC in appropriate clinical context
AFP-L3 and DCP not widely available in UK

system.name: BCLC
system.endorsement: Recommended for staging and treatment allocation in the UK

stages.stage: Single nodule less than 2 cm, preserved liver function, PS 0
Single or up to 3 nodules each less than 3 cm, preserved liver function, PS 0
Portal invasion and/or extrahepatic spread, preserved liver function, PS 1-2

liver_function.portal_hypertension: Platelet count less than 100,000/mcL suggests clinically significant portal hypertension

surgical_resection.indication: BCLC 0/A with preserved liver function, no clinically significant portal hypertension
surgical_resection.future_liver_remnant: Minimum 40% FLR required for safe resection in cirrhotic patients

approaches.approach: Laparoscopic resection may offer benefits (shorter hospital stay, less decompensation)
Portal vein embolisation for insufficient FLR

uk_criteria.milan: Single tumour up to 5 cm or up to 3 tumours each up to 3 cm, no vascular invasion
uk_criteria.ucsf: Single tumour up to 6.5 cm or up to 3 tumours with largest up to 4.5 cm and total diameter up to 8 cm

extended.single_tumour: Up to 5 cm with 6-month observation period demonstrating stable disease
extended.multiple_tumours: Up to 5 lesions, each up to 3 cm
extended.large_single: 5-7 cm with 6-month observation period demonstrating no progression

liver_transplantation.bridging: Recommended for patients with expected wait time greater than 6 months
liver_transplantation.downstaging: May be considered for patients exceeding criteria who respond to locoregional therapy

ablation.indication: BCLC 0/A, tumours up to 3 cm, not suitable for resection or transplant

modality.name: RFA
modality.efficacy: Complete ablation in greater than 90% for tumours less than 3 cm

modality.name: MWA
modality.efficacy: Similar or superior to RFA, less affected by heat-sink
modality.note: May allow treatment of larger tumours up to 5 cm

variants.deb_tace: Drug-eluting bead TACE - no proven survival advantage over conventional
variants.bland_embolisation: TAE without chemotherapy - comparable outcomes in some studies

refractoriness.criteria: Failure to achieve objective response after 2 TACE sessions

tare.indication: Alternative to TACE for BCLC B, particularly for large or infiltrative tumours
May be considered for BCLC C with segmental portal vein invasion
tare.personalised_dosimetry: Higher tumour doses (greater than 205 Gy) associated with improved outcomes

sbrt.indication: Alternative to ablation when ablation not feasible
sbrt.note: Limited UK experience, consider in specialist centres

regimen.name: Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab
regimen.indication: First-line for advanced HCC (BCLC C) or TACE-refractory, Child-Pugh A
regimen.requirement: EGD within 6 months to assess variceal risk before bevacizumab

regimen.name: Durvalumab plus Tremelimumab
regimen.regimen_detail: STRIDE regimen: single priming dose of tremelimumab 300mg plus durvalumab 1500mg, then durvalumab monotherapy every 4 weeks
regimen.advantage: Alternative for patients with contraindication to bevacizumab

regimen.name: Sorafenib
regimen.role: Reserved for patients ineligible for immunotherapy

regimen.name: Lenvatinib
regimen.dose: 12 mg daily for weight greater than or equal to 60 kg, 8 mg daily for weight less than 60 kg
regimen.role: Alternative first-line option if immunotherapy not suitable

regimen.name: Cabozantinib
regimen.indication: Second or third line after prior systemic therapy

regimen.name: Ramucirumab
regimen.indication: Second line with AFP greater than or equal to 400 ng/mL

child_pugh_b.note: Limited data for systemic therapy in Child-Pugh B
child_pugh_b.sorafenib_data: Median OS 5.2 months in Child-Pugh B7
child_pugh_b.recommendation: Consider on case-by-case basis for well-compensated B7

algorithm.bclc_a: Resection (if suitable) or ablation or liver transplant (if within criteria and suitable)
algorithm.bclc_b: TACE or TARE (consider systemic therapy if unsuitable or refractory)

multidisciplinary_care.recommendation: All HCC patients should be discussed at a specialist hepatobiliary MDT
multidisciplinary_care.impact: MDT management associated with improved treatment allocation and survival

palliative_care.indication: BCLC D stage, Child-Pugh C not suitable for transplant, ECOG PS 3-4
palliative_care.prognosis: Median survival 3-4 months with best supportive care

post_curative_treatment.imaging: CT or MRI every 3-4 months for first 2 years, then every 6 months
post_curative_treatment.afp: If elevated pre-treatment, monitor every 3 months

post_transplant.surveillance: CT chest/abdomen every 6 months for at least 5 years

on_systemic_therapy.response_assessment: RECIST 1.1 for systemic therapy, mRECIST for locoregional therapy
